title: Determinants and Inverse Matrices
seo_title: Determinants and Inverse Matrices Worksheet: Solve Systems with Matrices | 100 Questions
standard_text: Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on determinants and inverse matrices: 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 determinants, inverses, solving systems with A⁻¹B and area. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: det = ad − bc. A matrix has an inverse only when det ≠ 0.
body_html:
How it works

  • For abcd, the determinant is ad − bc.
  • For a 3 × 3 matrix, expand along the first row with signs + − +, using the 2 × 2 determinant left when you cross out each entry's row and column.
  • A square matrix has an inverse only if its determinant is not 0. For 2 × 2: A−1 = (1/det) · d−b−ca.
  • A system can be written AX = B. Then X = A−1B (multiply on the left).
Example

Find A−1 for A = 3152.

det = 3(2) − 1(5) = 1

Swap 3 and 2; change the signs of 1 and 5

Answer: 2−1−53

Example

Solve 3x + y = 7, 5x + 2y = 12.

X = A−1B = 2−1−53712

= 21

Answer: (2, 1)

Common mistakes

  • Computing ad + bc instead of ad − bc.
  • Forgetting to swap a and d or to change the signs of b and c.
  • Forgetting to divide by the determinant.
  • Multiplying BA−1. The inverse goes on the left.

faq.q: How do you find the determinant of a 2 × 2 matrix?
faq.a: Multiply the main diagonal and subtract the product of the other diagonal: ad − bc.

faq.q: When does a matrix have an inverse?
faq.a: A square matrix has an inverse exactly when its determinant is not 0.

faq.q: How do you find the inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix?
faq.a: Swap a and d, change the signs of b and c, and divide every entry by the determinant ad − bc.

faq.q: How do you solve a system with an inverse matrix?
faq.a: Write the system as AX = B, then multiply both sides on the left by A⁻¹: X = A⁻¹B.
